title: fix: harden Flux Vast maintenance cutovers
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Records the production cutover from maintenance-bound Vast instance `44731147` to `46491202`.
- Makes fresh Flux deployments isolated canaries by default; heartbeat and the production tunnel require explicit promotion.
- Hardens setup for CUDA compatibility paths, Hugging Face downloads, DNS fallback, and model-health gating.
- Adds direct canary verification through `CANARY_URL` before registry promotion.

Validation:
- `bash -n image.pollinations.ai/nunchaku/setup-vast.sh`
- `bash -n image.pollinations.ai/nunchaku/verify-vast.sh`
- `python3 -m py_compile image.pollinations.ai/nunchaku/server.py`
- Live production: 47 requests after cutover, all successful; four tunnel connections; old instance destroyed.

gist.headline: Canaries get their own nest
gist.blurb: Flux maintenance cutovers now send fresh GPU deployments through a proper little canary garden before they join production. The bees checked the tunnel, the model, and 47 live requests; nothing caught fire.
gist.summary: Hardened Flux Vast maintenance cutovers by moving production from instance 44731147 to 46491202, making new deployments isolated canaries by default, and requiring CANARY_URL verification plus explicit tunnel and registry promotion.
gist.impact: Flux image generation gains safer GPU maintenance transitions, with CUDA and Hugging Face setup fallbacks, model-health gates, and direct canary checks catching deployment trouble before traffic reaches a new instance.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy GPU garden cutover: Polli guides a small newly planted canary server toward a glowing production greenhouse only after it passes a heartbeat monitor, tunnel cable, and model-health check. Show the old server resting in the background, a new CRT-backed GPU node being verified, and code-plants/flowers to represent the hardened deployment path.
